title: A puzzling non-detection of [O III] and [C II] from a z ≈ 7.7 galaxy observed with ALMA
question: Characterize the ISM of the z=7.664 Lyman-alpha emitting galaxy z7_GSD_3811 via [O III] 88 um, [C II] 158 um and dust continuum, combined with rest-frame UV data, and compare with other high-redshift galaxies and local galaxies

data.angular_resolution: Continuum beams: band 6 0.87'' x 0.67'' (PA -81 deg); band 8 0.34'' x 0.25'' (PA -88 deg); tapered beams reach ~0.6'' (and ~1.1'' for [C II] with 0.5'' taper)
data.sensitivity: Continuum rms 26 uJy/beam (band 8, 87 um) and 9.9 uJy/beam (band 6, 152 um); collapsed line rms 23 (100 km/s) and 44 (400 km/s) mJy km/s/beam for [O III], 9.8 and 19 for [C II]

what.value: Lyman-alpha redshift, UV magnitude and target coordinates

evidence.quote: Coordinates from (cite: song_keck_2016), not corrected for offset between Gaia and HST.
ground based infrared photometry (VLT/HAWK-I Ks) from the CANDELS catalog
We have therefore used the coordinates from the Hubble Legacy Fields (HLF) GOODS-S catalog (cite: whitaker_hubble_2019)

what.value: z>6 galaxy compilation (UV magnitudes, IR luminosities, [C II] data) used for [C II]-SFR and IRX-beta comparisons

evidence.quote: from the recently published compilation by (cite: matthee_resolved_2019)

what.value: Local [C II]-SFR relations for HII/Starburst and metal-poor dwarf galaxies

evidence.quote: We also show the local relation for HII/Starburst galaxies and metal-poor dwarf galaxies from (cite: delooze_applicability_2014).

what.value: Local dwarf galaxy L[O III]/L_UV versus oxygen abundance compilation

evidence.quote: nearby dwarf galaxies originally from (cite: madden_overview_2013; delooze_applicability_2014; cormier_herschel_2015), compiled by (cite: inoue_detection_2016)

recipe.method: Standard pipeline calibration in CASA; executions from different cycles combined before imaging
key_parameters: Flux calibration uncertainty estimated from historical calibrator monitoring: ~30% band 8, ~10% band 6

recipe.goal: image cubes and continuum, with tapering
recipe.method: CASA clean with natural weighting; dirty image rms measured first, then cleaning threshold set to 2x rms; several spectral resolutions and tapers
key_parameters: natural weighting; tapers up to 0.35'' and 0.5'' ([C II]); spectral resolution from native to ~200 km/s
assumptions: [C II] emitting region may be 2-3 times larger than the UV component, motivating the 0.5'' taper

recipe.goal: search for line emission near the target
recipe.method: Visual inspection of cubes in velocity slices, then systematic search for pixels above 3x rms within 1'' of the target; moment-0 maps and spectra; imfit integrated SNR for brightest features
key_parameters: Search range -2000 to 700 km/s ([O III]) and -2900 to 1300 km/s ([C II]) relative to expected line position
5 sigma desired for a firm detection; marginal features also examined

recipe.goal: derive 3 sigma upper limits on [O III] and [C II] line luminosities
recipe.method: Integrated rms measured in images collapsed over 100 and 400 km/s around expected line positions; 3 sigma used as upper limit assuming unresolved source
key_parameters: Fiducial line FWHM 100 km/s, also 400 km/s
assumptions: Target unresolved with native beams; no continuum subtraction

recipe.goal: dust continuum upper limits and total IR luminosity
recipe.method: Continuum rms in full-band images after masking foreground source; modified black-body integrated over 8-1000 um with CMB correction; T_d 35 and 55 K as variations
assumptions: Dust temperature of 45 K and beta_d = 1.5 chosen to match other studies

recipe.goal: compare [C II] luminosity and SFR with local and high-z relations
recipe.method: UV and IR SFRs from Kennicutt & Evans relations; UV+IR SFR with IR 1 sigma limit as upper error bar; compare with Matthee et al. compilation rescaled to 100 km/s and De Looze local relations
key_parameters: T_d = 45 K for SFR_IR; velocity-integrated rms scales as sqrt(line width)
assumptions: UV magnitude error bars assumed symmetric and equal to the larger error

recipe.goal: place the target in the IRX-beta plane
recipe.method: UV slope from CANDELS F125W and F160W; IRX from 3 sigma band 6 L_IR upper limit; compared to Calzetti, SMC and ALPINE relations
key_parameters: T_d = 45 K, beta_d = 1.5 for L_IR; L_UV = nu L_nu at 1500 A rest-frame

recipe.goal: compare L[O III]/L_UV with high-z detections and local dwarfs
recipe.method: Compute L_UV for literature [O III] detections (with lensing magnification) and compare the L[O III]/L_UV upper limit with high-z objects and local dwarf galaxies versus oxygen abundance

recipe.goal: SED fitting with ALMA upper limits
recipe.method: PANHIT SED fit to HST/HAWK-I photometry plus ALMA [O III] and band 6/8 continuum upper limits, constant SFR, Chabrier IMF, GALAXEV stellar models, Calzetti attenuation
key_parameters: Redshift fixed to 7.664 and escape fraction zero; Z = 0.0001-0.02; A_V = 0-0.5 in steps of 0.05
7 data points, 4 fitted parameters, 3 degrees of freedom; age restricted to 300 Myr for the alternative solutions
assumptions: Constant SFR; [C II] upper limit not included

answer_key.quantity: [O III] 88 um and [C II] 158 um 3 sigma luminosity upper limits (100 km/s)

evidence.quote: with $3\sigma$ upper limits of $1.6 \ \times \ 10^{8} \ \mathrm{L_{\odot}}$ and $4.0 \ \times \ 10^{7} \ \mathrm{L_{\odot}}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: [O III] 3 sigma luminosity upper limit for 400 km/s line width

evidence.loc: 4.1 Upper limits for the [O III] and [C II] line fluxes
evidence.quote: $L_{\mathrm{[O iii]}} < 3.2 \ \times \ 10^{8} \  \mathrm{L_{\odot}}$

answer_key.quantity: [C II] 3 sigma luminosity upper limit for 400 km/s line width

evidence.loc: 4.1 Upper limits for the [O III] and [C II] line fluxes
evidence.quote: $L_{\mathrm{[C ii]}} < 7.5 \ \times \ 10^{7} \ \mathrm{L_{\odot}}$

answer_key.quantity: Collapsed [O III] image rms (100 and 400 km/s)

evidence.loc: 4.1 Upper limits for the [O III] and [C II] line fluxes
evidence.quote: The measured rms in our collapsed \[O iii\] images is $23$ and $44 \ \mathrm{mJy\ km \ s^{-1} \ beam^{-1}}$ for $\Delta v = 100$ and $400 \ \mathrm{km \ s^{-1}}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Collapsed [C II] image rms (100 and 400 km/s)

evidence.loc: 4.1 Upper limits for the [O III] and [C II] line fluxes
evidence.quote: For the corresponding \[C ii\] images, we measure an rms of $9.8$ and $19 \ \mathrm{mJy\ km \ s^{-1} \ beam^{-1}}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Continuum rms band 8 (87 um) and band 6 (152 um)

evidence.quote: The measured rms in the band 8 and band 6 continuum is 26 and 9.9 $\mathrm{\mu Jy \ beam}^{-1}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: 3 sigma total IR luminosity upper limits at 87 um and 152 um (T_d = 45 K)

evidence.loc: 4.2 Upper limits for the 87 um and 152 um dust continuum
evidence.quote: $L_{\mathrm{IR,87\mathrm{\mu m},45K}} \ <9.3 \ \times  \ 10^{10} \ \mathrm{L_{\odot}}$ and $L_{\mathrm{IR,152\mathrm{\mu m},45K}} <9.1 \ \times  \ 10^{10} \ \mathrm{L_{\odot}}$, respectively.
we find a UV SFR for z7_GSD_3811 of $\mathrm{SFR_{UV}} \ = \ 12_{-1}^{+1} \ \mathrm{M_{\odot}} \ \mathrm{yr^{-1}}$

answer_key.quantity: IR SFR upper limit (1 sigma, T_d = 45 K)

evidence.quote: we derive an IR SFR of $\mathrm{SFR_{IR}} \ < 4.5 \ \mathrm{M_{\odot}} \ \mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ ($1\sigma$) for a dust temperature of 45 K.
$\mathrm{SFR_{UV+IR}} \ = \ 12_{-1}^{+5} \ \mathrm{M_{\odot}} \ \mathrm{yr^{-1}}$
We obtain $\mathrm{log_{10}(IRX)} \lesssim 0.11$

answer_key.quantity: L[O III]/L_UV upper limit relative to MACS0416_Y1 and SXDF-NB1006-2

evidence.quote: is a factor $\sim 12$ and $\sim 5$ times lower than the ratio observed in MACS0416_Y1

answer_key.quantity: Mean oxygen abundance of local dwarfs with L[O III]/L_UV lower than the target

evidence.quote: The mean oxygen abundance of nearby dwarf galaxies with $L_{O iii} / L_{\mathrm{UV}}$ lower than z7_GSD_3811 is $\approx 9\%$ of the solar value.

answer_key.quantity: Metallicity upper limit from [C II] vs Vallini et al. 2015 relation (100 km/s)

evidence.quote: we find that the values we obtain are consistent with a metallicity of $Z\lesssim 0.08 \ \mathrm{Z_{\odot}}$ for a line-width of $\Delta v = 100 \ \mathrm{km \ s^{-1}}$.
this upper limit is relaxed to $Z\lesssim 0.12 \ \mathrm{Z_{\odot}}$

answer_key.quantity: Formal best-fit PANHIT solution (chi2_nu, age, Z)
answer_key.units: chi2_nu dimensionless; Gyr; Z as mass fraction

evidence.quote: Formally, the best-fitting solution ($\chi_{\nu}^2 \  = \ 3.40$) obtained from PANHIT gives a high age of $0.57 \ \mathrm{Gyr}$ and a low metallicity of $Z \ = \ 0.0004$.

answer_key.quantity: Best-fit PANHIT SFR and stellar mass

evidence.quote: The star formation rate of the model is $\mathrm{SFR} \ = \ 7.95 \  \mathrm{M_{\odot}yr^{-1}}$, with a stellar mass of $M_{\star} \ = \ 3.05 \times 10^{9} \ \mathrm{M_{\odot}}$

answer_key.value: Young: 2 Myr, Z = 0.0001; two older solutions at 0.29 Gyr with Z = 0.02 and Z = 0.0004

evidence.quote: Here we find a Young solution (with an age of $2 \ \mathrm{Myr}$) with low metallicity ($Z \ = \ 0.0001$), and two older solutions (with ages of $0.29 \ \mathrm{Gyr}$)
could indicate that z7_GSD_3811 has a low metallicity ($Z \lesssim 0.1 \ \mathrm{Z_{\odot}}$)

score_reason: Project codes, SPW setups, natural weighting, clean threshold, line widths, T_d, beta_d and numeric upper limits are given, but cell size, masks, flagging and PANHIT details are missing, so upper limits are approximately but not exactly reproducible.
rediscovery_reason: Both projects are named, the data are likely public, the recipe (natural weighting, 100 km/s collapse, 3 sigma limits) is simple enough to redo, and the main results are numeric upper limits.
